title: Define the canonical incident disposition and idempotent action contract

parentBehavior.description: Escalate only actionable failed-work incidents; unchanged owned or named-hold evidence stays quiet across ticks, restart, and replay.

problem: The Project reconciler can observe failed Work but has no canonical handled-failure fact or stable action identity, so unchanged owned correction can wake Astra or submit another action on every pass.
outcome: A reviewer can classify one incident as handled or actionable before Astra or recovery, append one immutable disposition fact through canonical Factory Events, rebuild the latest view from replay, and fail closed on unsafe or uncertain actions without changing Work state semantics.
sourcePlanRef: factory/docs/operating-policy.md#cadence-liveness-and-state; #failure-classification-and-escalation; #no-action-and-hold-policy; #executable-recovery-boundaries; requirement: stable fingerprint, handled check, selective escalation, and safe orphan repair
actorAndTrigger: Automations runs after public Factory Session, Work, Worker Session, and Factory Event reads during a scheduled or exception-triggered reconciliation pass.
sharedSurfaceOwnership: T002 owns the single Factory Event contract decision and identity/action semantics. Recordings owns append, validation, replay, and the latest projection; Automations owns classification/eligibility; Work and Factory Runtime own Work admission and move controls. T003 owns integrated matrix and rollout evidence.

in: Additive INCIDENT_DISPOSITION_RECORDED Factory Event vocabulary and payload proposal
Event-context requirements and stable fingerprint, event, and action identities
Disposition transitions, replay reduction, handled checks, selective escalation, external holds, concurrency, and lost-response semantics
Unowned, overdue, repeated-after-correction, stale-generation, active-execution, invalid-readiness, duplicate, malformed, partial-write, and valid-orphan outcomes
out: Generated clients, new incident endpoint, WorkRead field, Work state, historical backfill, or live event emission
Active Work/settings changes, LocalAI changes, provider/model calls, complete T003 matrix, clean-room repair, and rollout

constraints: Factory Work and Factory Events remain authoritative; incident disposition is event metadata and replay projection, never a Work state, filesystem queue, or second store.
Use the existing Recordings root Service.Append/canonical-ledger seam and public Work request/move controls; do not add a service locator, public root method, or endpoint in this packet.
Readers/projection precede writers; old recordings replay to an empty incident index; rollback stops new incident emission and preserves all history.
Reuse T001 normalization, exclude sweep timestamps/ticks/attempt IDs, bound and sanitize causal evidence, and reject malformed identity/context.
Lost or ambiguous public responses fail closed with a structured partial-write blocker; timer passage, idle capacity, or deterministic failure never justifies retry.

future contract, replay, and idempotence tests

identity.normalization: Trim values, lowercase ASCII identifiers, reject empty values, control characters, and pipe delimiters; exclude timestamps, ticks, and Worker Session attempts.
identity.collisionRule: Same ID and equivalent payload is idempotent; same ID with different payload is CONTRACT_CONFLICT and fails closed.

dispositionProtocol.latestOrder: Canonical Factory Event sequence; retain all historical events and failed Work.
handled: Same fingerprint/generation with correction-in-progress, owned nonterminal corrective Work, and future check.
Externally-blocked incident with named owner/hold before nextCheckAt/deadlineAt.
Verified-resolved while current public failure is absent.
An already recorded identical action/event identity.
actionable: Same causal failure after a new correction revision.
Valid orphan predicates after all safety checks.
failClosed: Unknown or contradictory metadata without a complete escalation witness.
Stale generation, active execution, invalid readiness, malformed metadata, duplicate conflict, or uncertain public readback.
dispositionProtocol.transitions: untriaged -> correction-in-progress|externally-blocked|verified-resolved; correction-in-progress -> itself|externally-blocked|verified-resolved; externally-blocked -> itself|correction-in-progress|verified-resolved; corrected repeat uses a new correction revision and retains prior history.

actionProtocol.dispositionOnly: Append the deterministic event through Recordings; on lost response reread by eventId and reuse the same event ID.
actionBearing: Reread by actionRequestId/eventId; exact accepted facts are ALREADY_RECORDED.
Submit one existing public Work Request or Work move with actionRequestId.
Reread public Work/Event acceptance, then append the exact disposition fact.
If accepted action is provable, reuse identity; if acceptance is uncertain, return PARTIAL_WRITE_UNCERTAIN and submit nothing more.
actionProtocol.concurrency: Concurrent passes converge on one external request ID and one event ID; no filesystem marker or in-memory lock is correctness state.

caseMatrix.given: M-04 evidence is unchanged on a second tick.
caseMatrix.then: Exact no-op counts; no timestamp-derived identity.

caseMatrix.then: One stable escalation; no failed-Work retry; repeat no-op.

caseMatrix.given: Same causal failure remains after correction revision.
caseMatrix.then: One new revision-scoped escalation; prior correction and failure history remain.
caseMatrix.observer: Action IDs, event history, and Work list.

caseMatrix.given: Named external hold has a future deadline.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Unchanged owned correction-in-progress evidence across two ticks, restart, and replay produces no new Astra request, retry, or disposition event while failed/history visibility remains.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Handled protocol and M-04/M-05/M-06 specify same-fingerprint projection, zero-action counts, replay reduction, and retained history.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Unowned, overdue, or repeated-after-correction evidence produces one stable revision-scoped escalation and unchanged repeats are no-ops.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Revision-scoped action formula, eligibility order, and M-07/M-08/M-09 define one request/event and stable repeat behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Stale generation, active execution, invalid readiness, duplicate request, partial write, and malformed metadata fail closed with structured reasons while Work/history are preserved.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Fail-closed protocol, lost-response rules, orphan predicates, and M-11 through M-16 define no-mutation outcomes.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Valid orphan predicates require the public move, WORK_STATE_CHANGE, and next-dispatch readback; failed Work remains failed.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Safe orphan repair section and M-17 require matching generation, no active execution/cycle, stable move identity, and public readback.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Lost append/action responses reuse the same identity when accepted state is public or return a partial-write blocker instead of creating a second request.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Action protocol defines public reread ordering, deterministic event/action IDs, same-ID conflict handling, and PARTIAL_WRITE_UNCERTAIN.

operationalAndRollout: No live Factory settings, active Work, event stream, generated output, or public endpoint changes. Future readers/projection precede writers; same-ID payload conflicts and partial-write uncertainty stop the action; rollback disables new writers and preserves history. Controlled rollout is a later Supervisor-owned gate.
escalation: Stop with a structured blocker if Recordings cannot validate reader-before-writer and same-ID conflict semantics, public Work admission/move cannot accept the stable request ID, readback cannot distinguish accepted from uncertain, or metadata requires a new Work state/endpoint. Include failed criterion, exact evidence, impact, safe work, owner, observable exit, and smallest delta.
